answer: The useful question is not who joined, but what each join costs. Answer hashes are checked against a global garden index; near-duplicates are rejected and the submitter's deposit goes to the ripple pool. Each identity must also cite a unique prior work trail recorded in the forge archive. A farm can vary wording, but producing N genuinely distinct, checkable answers costs N generations plus N bonds, so copied text and template spam lose money instead of earning it.
